subject: Dedicated capacity — throughput crediting proposal and queueing clarifications (Oakridge)
messages:
From: Dan Li <dan.li@oakridge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Tina Gomez <tina.gomez@oakridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool behavior — observed tail latency and request for crediting language

Hi Mina / Tina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We pushed a larger nightly job into the dedicated pool (32 reserved GPUs) and saw repeated tail-latency spikes during the 02:00–04:00 batch window — p95/token-latency roughly doubled versus the baseline in your published performance profile. The latency happens when many short inference jobs overlap with a few long-running streaming requests; it looks like queueing/backpressure rather than an outright outage.

We want to move forward but need two things clarified in the contract language before legal signs off:
- How Redwood defines and measures queueing-related SLA misses for Dedicated capacity (is this measured as reduced throughput, increased p95, or drop in successful requests?).
- Whether you will provide a crediting mechanism (throughput or time-based credits) when reserved capacity cannot sustain committed throughput because of internal queuing behavior. If yes, how will credits be calculated?

I've attached our draft SLA markup (see Oakridge_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) with proposed credit wording just to start the conversation. Can you propose a clear, objective crediting policy and an operational mitigation plan (e.g., carveouts, priority queues) that prevents this from recurring?

Can we get a 30–45 minute call early next week to align and capture the language your contracts team needs?

Best,
Dan
Dan Li
CTO, Oakridge AI
[Attachment: Oakridge_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF)]

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool behavior — observed tail latency and request for crediting language

Team — forwarding Oakridge's note. They hit a recurring tail latency pattern during a large nightly batch while on 32 reserved GPUs. External asks: 1) contract language for objective measurement of queueing-related SLA misses; 2) a crediting formula if we fail to sustain committed throughput; 3) operational mitigations to avoid recurrence (carveouts, queue priority, rate limiting).

A few constraints to keep in mind: Oakridge is on a Dedicated (reserved) pool and expects bounded tail latency for their steady-state production traffic. They also run heavy batch windows which can be scheduled but they want headroom/burst assurances.

Please review the attached usage CSV (dedicated_capacity_usage_q3.csv) for their recent profile. I need a proposed legal-friendly crediting clause and a short technical mitigation plan by EOD Monday so we can present options in the call.

Suggested deliverables:
- Marissa: customer-facing SLA language draft (one paragraph + calculation example).
- Vivek: technical note on queueing behavior and mitigations (priority carveouts, default rate limits, batching knobs).
- Rishi: ops playbook bullet points (measurement windows, metrics, rollback/fallback behavior).

Thanks — I'll handle scheduling with Dan after we have something to discuss.

Mina

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool behavior — proposed crediting language and examples

Mina / team — draft language below that I think is objective and reasonably conservative; I've also attached a redlined SLA (Oakridge_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf) with the example calculation filled in. Feedback welcome.

--- DRAFT SLA PARAGRAPH (proposed) ---
Redwood will maintain the committed Dedicated throughput for Oakridge AI measured as aggregate successful inference tokens processed per minute across the reserved pool during the measurement window. If, during any rolling 1-hour measurement window, the observed aggregate throughput falls below 95% of the committed throughput due to queueing behavior or resource contention in the reserved pool, Redwood will provide a throughput credit to Oakridge AI equal to:

  Credited amount (USD) = (Committed monthly capacity monthly_fee) * (Minutes_below_threshold / Total_minutes_in_month) * Credit_multiplier

Where:
- Minutes_below_threshold is the sum of minutes across the month where the rolling 1-hour aggregated throughput was <95% of committed.
- Credit_multiplier defaults to 1.5 for first-year commitments (can be negotiated).

Example: Oakridge committed 32 GPUs (equivalent to X throughput), monthly_fee = $120,000; observed Minutes_below_threshold = 120 minutes in the month => credit = $120,000 * (120/43,200) * 1.5 = $525.

Operational notes to include in the contract: Redwood will instrument per-tenant queue depth and per-job latency; Redwood will offer (at no additional cost during onboarding) a Burst Carveout option that reserves minimal concurrency headroom (configurable) for scheduled batch windows, and an optional Priority Queueing add-on to protect a percentage of reserved pool concurrency for production traffic.

--- end draft ---

I'm keeping the formula simple and auditable (throughput-based) rather than p95-only so the math ties directly to the customer's committed units. If we want to be stricter on latency we can add a parallel p95 credit metric, but that complicates measurement and dispute resolution.

Attaching Oakridge_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf with redlines and the example calculation.

Marissa
Head of Sales, Dedicated Capacity | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Oakridge_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool behavior — technical mitigations and measurement notes

On Mon, 02 Nov 2026 at 09:37 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Mina / team — draft language below that I think is objective and reasonably conservative; I've also attached a redlined SLA (Oakridge_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf) with the example calculation filled in. Feedback welcome.

Quick technical notes to pair with Marissa's draft:
- Root cause summary: the pattern Dan described matches contention between high-concurrency short requests and a few long-lived streaming calls. In our runtime, that leads to queue accumulation at the scheduler and then head-of-line blocking when the GPU batch scheduler fills on longer jobs.
- Measurement guidance: count "aggregate successful tokens per minute" using the tenant's reserved pool metrics (exclude queued-but-dropped requests). Correlate with per-tenant queue_depth and active_concurrency.
- Mitigations we can offer (configurable at onboarding):
  1) Burst Carveout: reserve N concurrency slots (e.g., 5 concurrent slots) that are only used for scheduled batch windows; these slots bypass general priority scheduling.
  2) Priority Queueing: tag production traffic with higher priority; implement preemption for low-priority batch jobs when production concurrency approaches threshold.
  3) Queue-depth alerts + auto-shed: if queue_depth > threshold for 5 consecutive minutes, shed or throttle low-priority jobs to maintain p95 targets.
  4) Per-tenant rate limiting and soft-fairness: enforce per-tenant token rates to prevent single-tenant burst storms.
- Testing: we should propose a short scheduled soak test with Oakridge where we reproduce their nightly profile and validate carveout sizing. This will let us fix the carveout number (N) and avoid overpromising.

I'll prepare a short 1-page technical note for the call with diagrams and a recommended default configuration for a 32-GPU pool.

Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Tina Gomez <tina.gomez@oakridge.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool behavior — throughput crediting proposal and queueing clarifications (Oakridge)

Dan — thanks for the clear write-up and for sharing the draft SLA. We've reviewed the usage logs and prepared the following:

1) Objective measurement: we propose using "aggregate successful inference tokens per minute" across the dedicated pool as the metric, measured with a rolling 1-hour window (matching Marissa's draft). We will provide per-tenant queue_depth and latency traces as supporting evidence.

2) Crediting policy: please review the attached redline (Oakridge_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf). Summary: credits are prorated based on minutes_below_threshold (rolling 1-hour window <95% committed throughput) with a default credit_multiplier of 1.5 for the first year. We included an example calculation to show impact.

3) Operational mitigations: Vivek recommends a two-pronged approach — a small Burst Carveout for scheduled batch windows (we suggest starting with 5 concurrency slots for your 32-GPU pool) plus Priority Queueing and auto-throttling for low-priority jobs. We also propose a 2-hour soak test (by mutual scheduling) to validate the carveout size before we finalize the SLA.

Next steps:
- If this direction looks acceptable, we'll send the redlined SLA and a short call agenda for a 45-minute alignment meeting.
- Proposed times: Wed Dec 2 or Thu Dec 3 (morning PST). Please reply with availability.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Mina Haddad
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
